clue.text: Persist in opposing project

definitions.meaning: to keep resisting, refusing to give way, is to hold or stand firm against
to jut or stick out beyond a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrasal-verb senses: to stay firm in resistance, and to protrude or jut prominently from a surface.

clue.text: Tried and succeeded opening box of treasure

indicators.note: this letter opens the word, coming first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
a trove is a store or cache of treasure

explanation.surface: Someone tried and managed to open a treasure chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning tried hard or endeavoured.

clue.text: Not many? Wrong, the opposite

indicators.note: the letters are put in a wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims there are few, and is told the reverse is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Woman briefly brought in to eliminate versatile competitor

indicators.note: one piece is brought inside the other

parts.note: to delete is to remove or eliminate
Cath is a short form of the woman's name Catherine

explanation.surface: A female substitute is drafted in to knock out an all-round athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlete competes in ten track and field events, so needs all-round ability.

clue.text: Class in local university initially teaching nothing at all

indicators.note: this piece comes at the start of the answer
one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a native is a local, someone born in the place
a form is a class at a British school

explanation.surface: A class at the nearby university starts out teaching nobody anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group; 'initially' puts the university first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uninformative gives no useful information, so it teaches nothing.

clue.text: Operate tape showing victory secured by socialist

indicators.note: a thing secured by something is held inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of a socialist
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A campaign recording plays the tape of a left-wing candidate's election triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a cassette backwards to its start is one specific way of operating the tape.

clue.text: Final signs of summertime: collared dove in garden

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Late summer brings a collared dove into the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: One married couple taken round a cleric's office

indicators.note: the outer pair is taken around the inner pair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: A newly-wed pair are shown round a priest's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' wraps I and MATE round MA.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the office or rank held by an imam, a Muslim prayer leader.

clue.text: Rock event: look to beat time

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: beaten letters are knocked about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: At a rock concert a drummer looks to keep time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a carbonate mineral and the sedimentary rock made from it.

clue.text: Rubbish put back in incinerators

indicators.note: something put back goes the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left
the letters sit inside the single clue word incinerators

explanation.surface: Garbage is returned to the furnaces for burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless talk is called rot, a colloquial synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Start of confrontation when allies bombed barrier

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word confrontation is taken
something bombed is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military clash begins when allied air forces bomb a defensive wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombed' rearranges WHENALLIES into HINESEWALL, placed after C.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the great defensive wall in northern China, and also of an information barrier within a firm.

clue.text: Remember a comic losing heart when performing? Not him, surely

definitions.text: Remember a comic losing heart when performing? Not him, surely

indicators.note: a performance puts things into action, so these letters are rearranged
the middle letter of comic is removed

explanation.surface: Could you forget a comedian who lost heart on stage? Not this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the M of COMIC; 'when performing' rearranges REMEMBERACOIC. Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Morecambe was a beloved British television comedian unlikely ever to be forgotten.

clue.text: Small volume -— in any case, it's just a novel

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for volume

indicators.note: a case holds things, so the word any wraps round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
the word it, with the 's standing for 'is' as a link
just means fair, as in equitable

explanation.surface: A little book is described, whatever its form, as merely a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' makes ANY hold IT, giving ANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's satirical Victorian work of fiction bears this title.

clue.text: Friendly crowd, except for leader

indicators.note: the word for crowd is used without its first letter

parts.note: a swarm is a thronging crowd

explanation.surface: A sociable gathering includes everyone but the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for leader' drops the S from SWARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a friendly, cordial one; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Novel way to summon artist

parts.note: to page someone is to summon them, e.g. over a speaker
J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Someone describes an original method of calling a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a gripping book, especially a novel, that readers can't put down.

clue.text: First of mysteries penned by more talented thriller writer

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: abler means more capable or more talented

indicators.note: only the opening letter of mysteries is used

explanation.surface: A mystery novelist's opening book is written by a superior suspense author.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was an English author of spy and suspense novels such as The Mask of Dimitrios.

clue.text: Most miserable, finding drink running short at home

indicators.note: the drink's name falls short by losing its last letter

parts.note: mead is a drink made from fermented honey
a nest is a home, as in a family nest

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest finds their alcohol supply dwindling at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' trims MEAD to MEA. 'Miserable' here means stingy, as in miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean means miserly or stingy, so the superlative fits the miserly sense of miserable.

clue.text: Town with once-fashionable street in Jersey, perhaps

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the word for the animal

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, so a cow is an example
hep is a dated word for trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: A town is linked with a formerly trendy road on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island but is the cattle breed. Chepstow is a Welsh border town known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a market town in Monmouthshire, south-east Wales.

clue.text: Part of leg, initially very delayed, at each meal

indicators.note: the word's first letter is held back and moved to the end

parts.note: the thigh is the upper part of the leg

explanation.surface: An injured leg holds up the traveller at every dining stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially very delayed' moves the T of THIGH to the end, giving HIGHT. HIGH TEA is a British early-evening meal with tea and cooked food.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a substantial late-afternoon or early-evening meal served with tea in Britain.

clue.text: Fellow has weapon inside coat, say

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or fellow
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A man has a gun concealed in his coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is one example of a garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Umpire always returned jacket

indicators.note: the whole run of letters is turned to read backwards

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An official keeps sending back a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket, originally worn by sailors.

clue.text: Learner goes into gym after test, for instance

indicators.note: this piece comes after the test in the answer

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: A student heads to the gym once the exam is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' puts L in PE, giving PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is an instance, and the phrase for example is used just like for instance.

clue.text: Extremely rare tax break

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of rare are taken

parts.note: a cess is a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tax break is very uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break or pause, as in a parliamentary or school recess.

clue.text: Tip showing how to make coffee

definitions.meaning: a perquisite or gratuity, an extra benefit

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a fringe benefit or extra; the other is short for percolate, the brewing method.

clue.text: Put off recording the 21st century

parts.note: a disc is a sound recording, a record or CD
the current era is our age

explanation.surface: Someone is deterred from making a recording about modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage is to dishearten or deter, the same as to put someone off.

clue.text: River going through one stretch of land

indicators.note: the letter goes through the middle of the other word

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A river runs across a piece of countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, so a measured stretch of land.

clue.text: Hearty eater's right to tuck into fish and tongue, skipping starter

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside another

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the language's name loses its first letter

parts.note: a tongue is a language, here German

explanation.surface: A glutton has every right to dig into fish and tongue, missing out the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' puts R in TENCH; 'skipping starter' cuts GERMAN to ERMAN. 'tuck into' and 'starter' play on eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencherman, from the wooden trencher plate, is someone who eats heartily.

clue.text: Author producing odd pieces of prose

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of prose are taken

explanation.surface: A writer produces scraps of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American writer of tales and poems such as The Raven.

clue.text: Royal attendants thus seen to droop

parts.note: attendants are those who are with someone, accompanying them
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch's servants appear to sag.
explanation.walkthrough: Those attending the Queen are with her, ER coming after, which 'thus' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and wilt, like a plant that droops.

clue.text: Perhaps people using rope to restrain stray dogs

indicators.note: the outer word holds the inner one in, like a restraint

parts.note: people who tie with rope are tiers
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Dog catchers use ropes to hold back stray dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' looks like an adjective describing the dogs, but here it is the verb meaning to wander off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers are a group of small, lively dog breeds originally bred for hunting.
